If the business takes **bookings** rather than orders (a salon, a tutor), it says so plainly and doesn't build a half-working shop. | 124 | 2 | **Review** | Seller | The profile appears as an ordinary form. The seller fixes anything wrong, adds photos, picks one of six looks and an accent colour, and sees a private live preview. No AI involved. | 125 | 3 | **Pick a name** | Claude + code | Claude suggests about ten names. Code checks which are really available and what they cost, and shows the best three. (Today, real launches use a free `.launchwitness.com` address.) | 126 | 4 | **Approve** | Seller | One card shows every step, every setting as **before → after**, and the exact cost. **Nothing is bought or changed until the seller taps Approve.** | 127 | 5 | **Launch** | Code only | Back up the current DNS settings, point the address at the server, set up email, turn the site on with HTTPS. Each step streams on screen and is logged. | 128 | 6 | **Prove** | Code (+ Claude to explain) | Run every check, including a real test order. Anything that fails goes to the Doctor, gets a safe fix, and is checked again. | 129 | 7 | **Report and watch** | Code | A report with every check, its result and time, the Doctor's explanations, and the full audit log. A shareable read-only link. Monitoring starts. | 130 131 After launch the seller also gets an **Orders** page (New → Confirmed → Paid → Done / Cancelled, with a one-tap WhatsApp message to the customer, and a "Customer says paid" note when a customer sends their UPI reference), new-order emails at their personal address, and an account page where they can delete everything. 132 133 --- 134 135 ## What "proven" means 136 137 Most tools would call a site "live" once the page loads. LaunchWitness is stricter. Each claim on the report comes from a stored `Evidence` row, and each hop is recorded separately: 138 139 | Check | How it's proven | Why it's done this way | 140 |---|---|---| 141 | **The address leads to the shop** | Asked of the domain's **own authoritative nameservers** (found from its NS records), not a cached resolver. The answering server is recorded. Google, Cloudflare and Quad9 are also asked, as information only. | Cached resolvers can show old answers for hours. The authoritative answer is the truth. | 142 | **The shop opens securely** | An HTTPS request with full certificate validation, **and** the page must carry the shop's own `` marker. | A parked page with a valid certificate would otherwise pass. | 143 | **Email settings are right** | MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC are looked up. The email provider is recognised from the domain's mail servers, and advice only ever uses that provider's values. | A missing setting silently sends orders to spam. | 144 | **A real order arrives** | The checker opens the public shop page, finds the order form and submits it exactly like a customer would (same fields, same form token), carrying a one-time code. Then it records: *form accepted* → *mail server accepted* (with message id) → *in the inbox* (read over IMAP, for mailboxes the app holds) **or** *owner confirmed* (a single-use "Yes, I got it" link inside the test email). | This is the whole point: the path a customer's order takes, tested end to end. | 145 | **The launch finished cleanly** | The step log shows every step done. | A half-finished launch can be resumed or undone. | 146 147 Two rules keep the report honest: 148 149 - **"Accepted" is never shown as "delivered".** Until the order is seen in the inbox or the owner confirms it, the report says something like "6 of 7 proven, 1 needs you" and the headline is "Almost ready". 150 - **"Not sure" is allowed. A wrong answer is not.** Every finding says how sure it is: *seen*, *not seen*, or *couldn't check*. If a lookup fails on our side, that is "couldn't check": never a pass, never the seller's fault, never an alert. 151 152 **The evidence is tamper-evident.** Each shop's evidence rows form an append-only hash chain (`app/chain.py`), written only through one function (`proof.add`). Anyone with the shared report link can press **Verify** (or call `GET /r//verify`), and the server recomputes the chain and says either "Intact" or exactly which saved step changed. 153 154 --- 155 156 ## The Doctor: fixing what breaks 157 158 Launches go wrong in ordinary ways: settings that haven't spread yet, a certificate that fails first time, a mailbox that isn't ready, a step that stops halfway. The Doctor handles these. 159 160 **How it works:** 161 162 1. A check fails. 163 2. For an address, padlock or test-order failure, the Doctor (Claude, cheap model) may first **investigate** using five **read-only** tools: `resolve` (the shop's own address), `fetch` (the shop's own page, through the SSRF guard), `evidence` (the stored proof of this run), `smtp_test` (connect and sign in to the mail server, never send) and `mailbox_status`. It gets at most 4 looks. 164 3. It answers with a finding in one plain sentence and **either** a fix id from the playbook **or** "needs you" with plain instructions for the owner. 165 4. **Code** checks the answer and is the only thing that acts. 166 167 **The playbook is five fixes, fixed in code** (`backend/app/agents/playbook.py`): 168 169 | Fix | What it does | 170 |---|---| 171 | `restore_backup` | Put every setting this launch touched back exactly as it was before (undo). Needs the owner. | 172 | `readd_mx` | Re-add the mail-server setting from the approved plan. | 173 | `readd_email_auth` | Re-add the SPF / DKIM / DMARC settings from the approved plan. | 174 | `retry_certificate` | Ask for the HTTPS certificate again. | 175 | `repoint_site` | Point the address at the shop again. | 176 177 **Limits:** at most 3 attempts per check, no fix ever spends money, and every attempt is written to the audit log. A fix the model suggests that isn't in the playbook, or isn't allowed for that check and launch type, is refused and logged. If Claude is unavailable or over budget, plain rules decide instead: if exactly one fix is allowed it is applied and labelled "Standard fix", otherwise the owner gets clear instructions. 178 179 On the report, each investigation is shown as a short timeline: *Looked up where your address leads → it leads nowhere → Pointed your address at your shop again → Checked again: working.* 180 181 **Describe the problem:** an owner can also type what they or a customer saw ("my customer says the page won't open"). Every check runs again and their words go to the Doctor, fenced off as data so they can't be used as instructions. 182 183 --- 184 185 ## Keeping watch after launch 186 187 GoDaddy's APIs have no webhooks, so LaunchWitness re-runs its checks on a timer: 188 189 | How often | What is checked | 190 |---|---| 191 | **Every 15 minutes** | The site opens, HTTPS is valid, the shop marker is present. | 192 | **Daily** | Address and email settings still match the launch; days left on the certificate and domain; a fresh test order, sent to LaunchWitness's own check mailbox (never to the owner) and found there over IMAP; answers from three public resolvers. | 193 | **On demand** | "Run checks now" on the report. | 194 195 Rules it follows: 196 197 - **A seller only gets a test email when she asked for one** (at launch, "Run checks now" or "Describe the problem"). Every test email's subject starts with `TEST, not a real order:` and opens with a grey "This is a check" banner, with no customer call or WhatsApp buttons. Test orders never appear on the Orders page or count against her daily limit. 198 - A failure is re-checked a minute later to rule out a blip before anything happens. 199 - Something that needs money or the owner's action (a renewal) is an **alert only**, sent 30, 7 and 1 days ahead. 200 - A check that has been fixed 3 times in a day and breaks again is no longer fixed automatically. The owner gets one "keeps breaking" email. 201 - Alerts go to the owner's **personal email**, through an outbox that saves every email first and retries with growing waits, so an order is never lost even if the mail server is down. 202 - Shops are checked side by side by a small worker pool, each at its own minute, with a 150-second watchdog per check. 203 204 **Watch this address:** signed-in users can also have any website (not just their shop) checked daily and get an email when something new goes wrong. Outside addresses are only ever *explained*, never changed. 205 206 --- 207 208 ## The shop itself 209 210 Every seller's site comes from **one rendering engine and one template**, server-rendered by FastAPI with Jinja2 and chosen by the `Host` header. There is no generated code and no per-seller CSS. 211 212 - **Six looks** for home businesses: Bakery & desserts, Home kitchen / tiffin, Handmade & crafts, Tailoring & custom work, Gifts & hampers, General. Claude picks only a **key** (which look, which accent, three short lines of copy). Code validates the key and draws everything: colours, self-hosted fonts, layout and illustrations. 213 - **Menu with prices in ₹**, a basket that works even without JavaScript, extras listed separately, a search box for long menus. 214 - **Order form** with date (minimum notice enforced), pickup or delivery (by area or PIN code), time slots, quantities, and totals worked out **on the server**. 215 - **Payment by UPI, only after an order**: the shop page never shows the seller's UPI ID or QR code. After a real order, the thank-you page (and the order's own private status page) shows "Pay ₹X via UPI" as a prefilled UPI link on phones and a QR code on laptops, with the exact amount and the order ID as the note. Pay-on-delivery orders get no UPI details at all. Money goes straight from the customer to the seller. It never passes through LaunchWitness. 216 - **"I've paid"**: after paying in their own UPI app, the customer can enter the 12-digit UPI reference (UTR) and, optionally, a screenshot (re-encoded, no hidden data). The seller sees **"Customer says paid"**, never "Paid": they check their own UPI app and mark the order Paid themselves. References and screenshots are private to the seller, and are deleted 30 days after the order closes. 217 - **Each shop's own signature**: a small set of drawings (sprinkles, leaves, stars and so on) chosen by code from the shop's name, shown as a strip under the top of the page where no text sits, plus gentle touches (add-to-basket, a quick view of each item). The page works the same with JavaScript off. 218 - **WhatsApp button**, an order status page per order, a privacy page, "Report this shop", and the optional food licence (FSSAI) number. 219 - **Product photos**: re-encoded to WebP from the pixels alone, so no location or camera data survives. 220 - **Accessibility and safety**: every colour combination passes WCAG AA (tested), every seller-supplied field is HTML-escaped (tested with hostile input in every field, in every look), and shop pages send a strict Content-Security-Policy. 221 222 Screenshots of every look: [`docs/screenshots/s14/contact-sheet.png`](docs/screenshots/s14/contact-sheet.png). 223 224 --- 225 226 ## Safety: why an AI can be trusted with this 227 228 The core rule: **the model decides and explains; plain code acts and checks.** 229 230 | Rule | How it's enforced | 231 |---|---| 232 | **Approve before spending** | A purchase in code needs **all three**: `ALLOW_PURCHASE=true` (off by default), a cost under the hard cap `MAX_SPEND_USD`, and a matching approval record from the owner. In practice, domains are bought by the owner on godaddy.com and then adopted. | 233 | **Preview before changing** | Every DNS change is shown as before → after on the approval card. | 234 | **Back up, then undo** | The current records are saved before any DNS write. A write without a backup is refused. A failed launch can be put back. | 235 | **Scoped writes** | A launch can only touch its own domain (or its own subdomain), one record type and name at a time. DNS is never written to a domain that isn't in the app's own database. | 236 | **Fixed repairs** | The Doctor can only choose from five fixes in code. Anything else is refused and logged. | 237 | **Everything audited** | Every change of state writes an `AuditEvent` (who, what, when, result), shown in the report. | 238 | **Sandbox by default** | `GODADDY_ENV=ote` (GoDaddy's test environment) unless production is set explicitly. | 239 | **No secrets in the repo** | All keys come from environment variables. `.env` exists only on the server. A secret scan of the repo and the whole git history is clean. | 240 | **Trust and safety for a public tool** | Sign-in by email link (no passwords); team approval before an account can launch for real; a Claude policy check that can only **hold** a shop for human review, never launch one (and holds if it fails); "Report this shop"; a team pause switch; rate limits per visitor and per account; a cap of 40 live shops. | 241 242 --- 243 244 ## How GoDaddy is used 245 246 GoDaddy is the engine, not decoration. 247 248 | Step | GoDaddy product | What LaunchWitness does with it | 249 |---|---|---| 250 | **Find a name** | Domains API | Availability and price for the names Claude suggests. | 251 | **Buy** | godaddy.com checkout | Done by the owner, then adopted after approval. The API purchase path exists but is locked behind the spend guards. | 252 | **Point and protect** | DNS API | Back up the zone; write scoped records (A, MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC); undo from backup. All calls share one rate limit (50 a minute, under GoDaddy's 60). | 253 | **Email** | GoDaddy Professional Email (Titan) | The app's mailbox sends every email over SMTP (`smtpout.secureserver.net`) and reads the inbox over IMAP to prove a test order arrived. | 254 | **Host** | GoDaddy Docker VPS | Runs everything. Caddy issues an HTTPS certificate for each shop on demand, but only for domains in the app's database. | 255 | **Verify** | GoDaddy's authoritative nameservers | Checks ask GoDaddy's own nameservers, not a cache, so the result is the real one. | 256 257 Hosting is the Docker VPS, not GoDaddy's Hosting API: one box runs the app and every seller site with automatic HTTPS. 258 259 --- 260 261 ## How Claude is used 262 263 Claude has three jobs, and none of them involve acting on money or DNS. 264 265 | Role | Model | Job | Output | 266 |---|---|---|---| 267 | **Reader** | Strong (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, vision) | Turn a messy description and price list (text or photo, English or Hinglish) into a strict profile, the shop's wording, and its look. Decide whether the business takes orders or bookings. | Profile JSON. Code tidies and validates every field. | 268 | **Namer** | Cheap (`claude-haiku-5-5`) | Suggest about ten names that fit the brand. | Names. Code checks availability and price. | 269 | **Doctor** | Cheap | Investigate a failed check with read-only tools and explain it in one sentence. | A finding plus a playbook fix id or "needs you". Code applies it. | 270 | **Policy check** | Cheap | Is this shop OK to put live? | OK, or "hold for review" with a reason. It can never launch or unpause. | 271 272 **Cost:** roughly 3 calls per launch plus 1 per failed check, a few cents in total. Every call has a tight `max_tokens`, and a daily spend cap stops live calls when reached. During development, saved responses ("fixtures") in `backend/tests/fixtures/` replace live calls, so the UI was built at $0 of API spend. Seller text and tool results are always passed as data, and a prompt-injection fixture is part of the test suite. 273 274 --- 275 276 ## Architecture 277 278 ``` 279 ┌──────────────── GoDaddy Docker VPS ─────────────────┐ 280 │ │ 281 browser / phone ───▶ │ Caddy │ 282 (app, shops, │ • HTTPS for the app and every shop │ 283 shared reports) │ • on-demand TLS, approved by an internal "ask" │ 284 │ endpoint (only domains in the database) │ 285 │ │ │ 286 │ ▼ │ 287 │ FastAPI app (one process) │──▶ GoDaddy Domains / DNS APIs 288 │ • JSON API + the built React app │──▶ Claude API 289 │ • seller shops (Jinja2, picked by Host header) │ (Reader, Namer, Doctor, policy) 290 │ • agents: Planner, Executor, Checker (code) │──▶ SMTP / IMAP (app mailbox) 291 │ • Doctor playbook (code) │──▶ public DNS + HTTPS probes 292 │ • outbox (every email saved, then retried) │ (through the SSRF guard) 293 │ • APScheduler monitoring + worker pool │ 294 │ • SQLite (WAL) on a volume, nightly backups │ 295 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 296 ``` 297 298 ### The agents 299 300 | Agent | Claude or code | Job |

Anything that fails goes to the Doctor, gets a safe fix, and is checked again. | | 7 | **Report and watch** | Code | A report with every check, its result and time, the Doctor's explanations, and the full audit log. A shareable read-only link. Monitoring starts. | After launch the seller also gets an **Orders** page (New → Confirmed → Paid → Done / Cancelled, with a one-tap WhatsApp message to the customer, and a "Customer says paid" note when a customer sends their UPI reference), new-order emails at their personal address, and an account page where they can delete everything. --- ## What "proven" means Most tools would call a site "live" once the page loads. LaunchWitness is stricter. Each claim on the report comes from a stored `Evidence` row, and each hop is recorded separately: | Check | How it's proven | Why it's done this way | |---|---|---| | **The address leads to the shop** | Asked of the domain's **own authoritative nameservers** (found from its NS records), not a cached resolver. The answering server is recorded. Google, Cloudflare and Quad9 are also asked, as information only. | Cached resolvers can show old answers for hours. The authoritative answer is the truth. | | **The shop opens securely** | An HTTPS request with full certificate validation, **and** the page must carry the shop's own `` marker. | A parked page with a valid certificate would otherwise pass. | | **Email settings are right** | MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC are looked up. The email provider is recognised from the domain's mail servers, and advice only ever uses that provider's values. | A missing setting silently sends orders to spam. | | **A real order arrives** | The checker opens the public shop page, finds the order form and submits it exactly like a customer would (same fields, same form token), carrying a one-time code. Then it records: *form accepted* → *mail server accepted* (with message id) → *in the inbox* (read over IMAP, for mailboxes the app holds) **or** *owner confirmed* (a single-use "Yes, I got it" link inside the test email). | This is the whole point: the path a customer's order takes, tested end to end. | | **The launch finished cleanly** | The step log shows every step done. | A half-finished launch can be resumed or undone. | Two rules keep the report honest: - **"Accepted" is never shown as "delivered".** Until the order is seen in the inbox or the owner confirms it, the report says something like "6 of 7 proven, 1 needs you" and the headline is "Almost ready". - **"Not sure" is allowed. A wrong answer is not.** Every finding says how sure it is: *seen*, *not seen*, or *couldn't check*. If a lookup fails on our side, that is "couldn't check": never a pass, never the seller's fault, never an alert. **The evidence is tamper-evident.** Each shop's evidence rows form an append-only hash chain (`app/chain.py`), written only through one function (`proof.add`). Anyone with the shared report link can press **Verify** (or call `GET /r//verify`), and the server recomputes the chain and says either "Intact" or exactly which saved step changed. --- ## The Doctor: fixing what breaks Launches go wrong in ordinary ways: settings that haven't spread yet, a certificate that fails first time, a mailbox that isn't ready, a step that stops halfway. The Doctor handles these. **How it works:** 1. A check fails. 2. For an address, padlock or test-order failure, the Doctor (Claude, cheap model) may first **investigate** using five **read-only** tools: `resolve` (the shop's own address), `fetch` (the shop's own page, through the SSRF guard), `evidence` (the stored proof of this run), `smtp_test` (connect and sign in to the mail server, never send) and `mailbox_status`. It gets at most 4 looks. 3. It answers with a finding in one plain sentence and **either** a fix id from the playbook **or** "needs you" with plain instructions for the owner. 4. **Code** checks the answer and is the only thing that acts. **The playbook is five fixes, fixed in code** (`backend/app/agents/playbook.py`): | Fix | What it does | |---|---| | `restore_backup` | Put every setting this launch touched back exactly as it was before (undo). Needs the owner. | | `readd_mx` | Re-add the mail-server setting from the approved plan. | | `readd_email_auth` | Re-add the SPF / DKIM / DMARC settings from the approved plan. | | `retry_certificate` | Ask for the HTTPS certificate again. | | `repoint_site` | Point the address at the shop again. | **Limits:** at most 3 attempts per check, no fix ever spends money, and every attempt is written to the audit log. A fix the model suggests that isn't in the playbook, or isn't allowed for that check and launch type, is refused and logged. If Claude is unavailable or over budget, plain rules decide instead: if exactly one fix is allowed it is applied and labelled "Standard fix", otherwise the owner gets clear instructions. On the report, each investigation is shown as a short timeline: *Looked up where your address leads → it leads nowhere → Pointed your address at your shop again → Checked again: working.* **Describe the problem:** an owner can also type what they or a customer saw ("my customer says the page won't open"). Every check runs again and their words go to the Doctor, fenced off as data so they can't be used as instructions. --- ## Keeping watch after launch GoDaddy's APIs have no webhooks, so LaunchWitness re-runs its checks on a timer: | How often | What is checked | |---|---| | **Every 15 minutes** | The site opens, HTTPS is valid, the shop marker is present. | | **Daily** | Address and email settings still match the launch; days left on the certificate and domain; a fresh test order, sent to LaunchWitness's own check mailbox (never to the owner) and found there over IMAP; answers from three public resolvers. | | **On demand** | "Run checks now" on the report. | Rules it follows: - **A seller only gets a test email when she asked for one** (at launch, "Run checks now" or "Describe the problem"). Every test email's subject starts with `TEST, not a real order:` and opens with a grey "This is a check" banner, with no customer call or WhatsApp buttons. Test orders never appear on the Orders page or count against her daily limit. - A failure is re-checked a minute later to rule out a blip before anything happens. - Something that needs money or the owner's action (a renewal) is an **alert only**, sent 30, 7 and 1 days ahead. - A check that has been fixed 3 times in a day and breaks again is no longer fixed automatically. The owner gets one "keeps breaking" email. - Alerts go to the owner's **personal email**, through an outbox that saves every email first and retries with growing waits, so an order is never lost even if the mail server is down. - Shops are checked side by side by a small worker pool, each at its own minute, with a 150-second watchdog per check. **Watch this address:** signed-in users can also have any website (not just their shop) checked daily and get an email when something new goes wrong. Outside addresses are only ever *explained*, never changed. --- ## The shop itself Every seller's site comes from **one rendering engine and one template**, server-rendered by FastAPI with Jinja2 and chosen by the `Host` header. There is no generated code and no per-seller CSS. - **Six looks** for home businesses: Bakery & desserts, Home kitchen / tiffin, Handmade & crafts, Tailoring & custom work, Gifts & hampers, General. Claude picks only a **key** (which look, which accent, three short lines of copy). Code validates the key and draws everything: colours, self-hosted fonts, layout and illustrations. - **Menu with prices in ₹**, a basket that works even without JavaScript, extras listed separately, a search box for long menus. - **Order form** with date (minimum notice enforced), pickup or delivery (by area or PIN code), time slots, quantities, and totals worked out **on the server**. - **Payment by UPI, only after an order**: the shop page never shows the seller's UPI ID or QR code. After a real order, the thank-you page (and the order's own private status page) shows "Pay ₹X via UPI" as a prefilled UPI link on phones and a QR code on laptops, with the exact amount and the order ID as the note. Pay-on-delivery orders get no UPI details at all. Money goes straight from the customer to the seller. It never passes through LaunchWitness. - **"I've paid"**: after paying in their own UPI app, the customer can enter the 12-digit UPI reference (UTR) and, optionally, a screenshot (re-encoded, no hidden data). The seller sees **"Customer says paid"**, never "Paid": they check their own UPI app and mark the order Paid themselves. References and screenshots are private to the seller, and are deleted 30 days after the order closes. - **Each shop's own signature**: a small set of drawings (sprinkles, leaves, stars and so on) chosen by code from the shop's name, shown as a strip under the top of the page where no text sits, plus gentle touches (add-to-basket, a quick view of each item). The page works the same with JavaScript off. - **WhatsApp button**, an order status page per order, a privacy page, "Report this shop", and the optional food licence (FSSAI) number. - **Product photos**: re-encoded to WebP from the pixels alone, so no location or camera data survives. - **Accessibility and safety**: every colour combination passes WCAG AA (tested), every seller-supplied field is HTML-escaped (tested with hostile input in every field, in every look), and shop pages send a strict Content-Security-Policy. Screenshots of every look: [`docs/screenshots/s14/contact-sheet.png`](docs/screenshots/s14/contact-sheet.png). --- ## Safety: why an AI can be trusted with this The core rule: **the model decides and explains; plain code acts and checks.** | Rule | How it's enforced | |---|---| | **Approve before spending** | A purchase in code needs **all three**: `ALLOW_PURCHASE=true` (off by default), a cost under the hard cap `MAX_SPEND_USD`, and a matching approval record from the owner. In practice, domains are bought by the owner on godaddy.com and then adopted. | | **Preview before changing** | Every DNS change is shown as before → after on the approval card. | | **Back up, then undo** | The current records are saved before any DNS write. A write without a backup is refused. A failed launch can be put back. | | **Scoped writes** | A launch can only touch its own domain (or its own subdomain), one record type and name at a time. DNS is never written to a domain that isn't in the app's own database. | | **Fixed repairs** | The Doctor can only choose from five fixes in code. Anything else is refused and logged. | | **Everything audited** | Every change of state writes an `AuditEvent` (who, what, when, result), shown in the report. | | **Sandbox by default** | `GODADDY_ENV=ote` (GoDaddy's test environment) unless production is set explicitly. | | **No secrets in the repo** | All keys come from environment variables. `.env` exists only on the server. A secret scan of the repo and the whole git history is clean. | | **Trust and safety for a public tool** | Sign-in by email link (no passwords); team approval before an account can launch for real; a Claude policy check that can only **hold** a shop for human review, never launch one (and holds if it fails); "Report this shop"; a team pause switch; rate limits per visitor and per account; a cap of 40 live shops. | --- ## How GoDaddy is used GoDaddy is the engine, not decoration. | Step | GoDaddy product | What LaunchWitness does with it | |---|---|---| | **Find a name** | Domains API | Availability and price for the names Claude suggests. | | **Buy** | godaddy.com checkout | Done by the owner, then adopted after approval. The API purchase path exists but is locked behind the spend guards. | | **Point and protect** | DNS API | Back up the zone; write scoped records (A, MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC); undo from backup. All calls share one rate limit (50 a minute, under GoDaddy's 60). | | **Email** | GoDaddy Professional Email (Titan) | The app's mailbox sends every email over SMTP (`smtpout.secureserver.net`) and reads the inbox over IMAP to prove a test order arrived. | | **Host** | GoDaddy Docker VPS | Runs everything. Caddy issues an HTTPS certificate for each shop on demand, but only for domains in the app's database. | | **Verify** | GoDaddy's authoritative nameservers | Checks ask GoDaddy's own nameservers, not a cache, so the result is the real one. | Hosting is the Docker VPS, not GoDaddy's Hosting API: one box runs the app and every seller site with automatic HTTPS. --- ## How Claude is used Claude has three jobs, and none of them involve acting on money or DNS. | Role | Model | Job | Output | |---|---|---|---| | **Reader** | Strong (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, vision) | Turn a messy description and price list (text or photo, English or Hinglish) into a strict profile, the shop's wording, and its look. Decide whether the business takes orders or bookings. | Profile JSON. Code tidies and validates every field. | | **Namer** | Cheap (`claude-haiku-5-5`) | Suggest about ten names that fit the brand. | Names. Code checks availability and price. | | **Doctor** | Cheap | Investigate a failed check with read-only tools and explain it in one sentence. | A finding plus a playbook fix id or "needs you". Code applies it. | | **Policy check** | Cheap | Is this shop OK to put live? | OK, or "hold for review" with a reason. It can never launch or unpause. | **Cost:** roughly 3 calls per launch plus 1 per failed check, a few cents in total. Every call has a tight `max_tokens`, and a daily spend cap stops live calls when reached. During development, saved responses ("fixtures") in `backend/tests/fixtures/` replace live calls, so the UI was built at $0 of API spend. Seller text and tool results are always passed as data, and a prompt-injection fixture is part of the test suite. --- ## Architecture ``` ┌──────────────── GoDaddy Docker VPS ─────────────────┐ │ │ browser / phone ───▶ │ Caddy │ (app, shops, │ • HTTPS for the app and every shop │ shared reports) │ • on-demand TLS, approved by an internal "ask" │ │ endpoint (only domains in the database) │ │ │ │ │ ▼ │ │ FastAPI app (one process) │──▶ GoDaddy Domains / DNS APIs │ • JSON API + the built React app │──▶ Claude API │ • seller shops (Jinja2, picked by Host header) │ (Reader, Namer, Doctor, policy) │ • agents: Planner, Executor, Checker (code) │──▶ SMTP / IMAP (app mailbox) │ • Doctor playbook (code) │──▶ public DNS + HTTPS probes │ • outbox (every email saved, then retried) │ (through the SSRF guard) │ • APScheduler monitoring + worker pool │ │ • SQLite (WAL) on a volume, nightly backups │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### The agents | Agent | Claude or code | Job |

300 | Agent | Claude or code | Job | 301 |---|---|---| 302 | **Reader** | Claude | Description + price list → profile + copy + look | 303 | **Namer** | Claude suggests, code checks | Available names with real prices | 304 | **Policy** | Claude decides, code holds | OK to go live, or hold for a human | 305 | **Planner** | Code | Every step, every before → after setting, and the cost → the approval card | 306 | **Executor** | Code | Runs the approved plan with the guards, backup first, resumable step log | 307 | **Checker** | Code | Address, HTTPS, email settings, real test order, clean finish | 308 | **Doctor** | Claude chooses, code applies | Investigate, explain, pick a playbook fix, re-check | 309 310 ### Design decisions worth knowing 311 312 - **Every outside service sits behind one wrapper with a fake.** GoDaddy, Claude, SMTP, IMAP, DNS and HTTPS each have a real and an in-memory implementation (`app/integrations.py`). Practice mode (`USE_FAKES=true`) and the whole test suite run against the fakes, and tests block every real network call. 313 - **Practice and real launches run the same code.** Practice swaps the outside world for fakes; the shop page, order handler and checks are identical, and every practice row is labelled. 314 - **One A record per shop, no wildcard.** Each real shop gets exactly one DNS record written by the app, so a shop that doesn't exist doesn't resolve. 315 - **SQLite on purpose.** One VPS, one app process (the app refuses to start a second), WAL mode, online backups (7 daily + 4 weekly) with a tested restore. Moving to Postgres is a small change because every table is a SQLModel model. 316 - **The checker can't be turned into a weapon.** It reaches websites only through `SafeWeb`: it resolves the host once, refuses private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses, pins the checked IP, and re-checks every redirect. 317 - **The app container uses public DNS resolvers.** The VPS's own resolvers returned wrong answers for some domains during testing, so the app asks 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 instead. 318 319 --- 320 321 ## Tech stack 322 323 | Layer | Technology | 324 |---|---| 325 | Backend | Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLModel + SQLite, httpx, dnspython, APScheduler, Jinja2, Pillow, segno (QR codes), `anthropic` SDK | 326 | Frontend | React 18, Vite 5, TypeScript, plain CSS (no UI kit) | 327 | Seller sites | Server-rendered Jinja2, one template, six themes, self-hosted open-licence fonts | 328 | Infrastructure | GoDaddy Docker VPS, Docker Compose, Caddy (automatic HTTPS, on-demand TLS) | 329 | Email | GoDaddy Professional Email over SMTP and IMAP; Mailpit for the local stack | 330 | Testing | pytest (1,580+ backend tests), Playwright end-to-end flows, ruff | 331 332 --- 333 334 ## Repository layout 335 336 ``` 337 backend/ 338 app/ 339 main.py FastAPI app, routers, host-based shop routing 340 config.py settings from environment variables 341 models.py, db.py SQLite tables (Business, Plan, DnsBackup, Evidence, AuditEvent, Approval, ...) 342 agents/ reader, namer, policy, doctor, investigator (Claude); 343 planner, executor, checker, launch_check, playbook (code) 344 checks/ DNS lookups, HTTPS probes, email-settings checks, SSRF-safe fetch 345 godaddy/ GoDaddy API client (ote|prod, scoped DNS writes), availability, email, rate limit 346 sites/ shop rendering, themes, orders, fulfilment rules, templates, fonts 347 mail/ SMTP, IMAP, email layout 348 monitor/ scheduler for light monitoring 349 safety/ spend guard, access control, CSRF/origin guard, route table 350 proof.py, chain.py evidence rows and the hash chain 351 outbox.py every email saved first, then sent and retried 352 routers/ API routes (auth, businesses, launch, report, admin, watch, ...) 353 tests/ pytest suite + fixtures (saved Claude responses, sample sellers) 354 frontend/ React + Vite app (landing, describe, review, launch, report, orders, admin) 355 e2e/ Playwright end-to-end tests 356 deploy/ Dockerfile, docker-compose files, Caddyfile (local) and Caddyfile.prod 357 scripts/ backups, checks, demo seeding, screenshots, secret scan, replay builder 358 docs/ spec, build plan, progress, build log, security, checks matrix, runbooks, screenshots 359 replay/ redacted Claude Code session transcripts (served at /build) 360 ``` 361 362 --- 363 364 ## Running it yourself 365 366 ### Option 1: practice mode on your machine (no keys needed) 367 368 Practice mode uses in-memory fakes for GoDaddy, DNS, the mailbox and HTTPS, and saved Claude responses, so you don't need any API keys. 369 370 ```bash 371 cp .env.example .env # defaults are safe: fakes on, sandbox, purchases off 372 python3.12 -m venv .venv 373 .venv/bin/pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt 374 (cd frontend && npm install && npm run build) 375 376 cd backend 377 ../.venv/bin/pytest -q # run the tests (no network) 378 ../.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000 379 ``` 380 381 Open http://localhost:8000. For local development set `DEV_MODE=true` in `.env` so sign-in links appear on screen instead of being emailed (it refuses to start on https). `cd frontend && npm run dev` runs the frontend with hot reload and proxies `/api` to port 8000. 382 383 > **On Windows**, use `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` and `.venv/Scripts/python -m uvicorn ...` instead. 384 385 ### Option 2: the full stack with Docker 386 387 ```bash 388 docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build # → http://localhost 389 ``` 390 391 A production-like stack (real HTTPS through Caddy's local certificate authority, `DEV_MODE=false`, fakes, and Mailpit to catch emails at http://localhost:8025): 392 393 ```bash 394 docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml \ 395 -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build --wait # → https://launchwitness.localhost 396 bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local # automated checks of the running stack 397 ``` 398 399 ### Option 3: production on a VPS 400 401 Follow [`docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`](docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md) and [`docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md`](docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md). In short: fill `.env` on the server (never in the repo), then 402 403 ```bash 404 docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build 405 bash scripts/check_m1.sh 406 ``` 407 408 Backups: `bash scripts/backup_db.sh` (7 daily + 4 weekly), restore with `bash scripts/restore_db.sh `. 409 410 ### Rehearsing the demo 411 412 ```bash 413 python3 scripts/seed_demo.py --launched # creates Meera's shop and runs a practice launch 414 python3 scripts/seed_demo.py --reset # removes it 415 ``` 416 417 To show the Doctor at work, sign in as the team (`ADMIN_EMAIL`), open a shop's report, and use the demo switch to stage a fault: the address leads nowhere, a parked page, a broken padlock, or a refused mail sign-in. The fault is staged so the demo is reliable; detecting and fixing it is real code. 418 419 ### Key environment variables 420 421 All are listed in [`.env.example`](.env.example) with safe defaults. 422 423 | Variable | Default | Meaning | 424 |---|---|---| 425 | `USE_FAKES` | `true` | Use in-memory fakes for every outside service | 426 | `GODADDY_ENV` | `ote` | GoDaddy sandbox; `prod` only when set explicitly | 427 | `ALLOW_PURCHASE` | `false` | Purchases are impossible unless turned on | 428 | `MAX_SPEND_USD` | `15` | Hard limit on any single purchase | 429 | `CLAUDE_MODE` | `fixture` | `fixture` uses saved responses; `live` calls the API | 430 | `CLAUDE_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` | `3` | Live Claude calls stop when reached | 431 | `DNS_MODE` | `per_shop` | One A record per shop (or `wildcard`) | 432 | `MONITOR_ENABLED` | `true` | Background monitoring (tests never start it) | 433 | `MAX_LIVE_SHOPS` | `40` | Upper limit on real shops | 434 435 --- 436 437 ## Testing 438 439 ```bash 440 cd backend && ../.venv/bin/pytest -q # 1,580+ tests, no network access allowed 441 .venv/bin/python -m ruff check backend # lint 442 cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build 443 cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npx playwright test 444 bash scripts/secret_scan.sh # secrets in the repo and the whole git history 445 ``` 446 447 What the tests cover, among other things: 448 449 - **Every check scenario** in [`docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md`](docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md): about forty website and email situations, each with the exact wording shown, how sure it is, and what the Doctor may do. 450 - **Access control:** every owner route tested as owner, another seller, a guest, logged out and admin. A test fails if any route is missing from the route table. 451 - **XSS:** a hostile string in every free-text field, every product field and the order form, parsed with a real HTML parser, in every theme. 452 - **SSRF:** private ranges, redirect re-checks, IP pinning, redirect loops. 453 - **Safety guards:** purchases blocked without all three conditions, DNS writes refused without a backup or outside the database. 454 - **The Claude agents** against saved real responses, including a prompt-injection seller and a handwritten price-list photo. 455 - **End-to-end flows** in a real browser: a full seller journey, two sellers who must not see each other's shops, guest practice, sign-in, legal pages, every theme launched in practice with no console errors or CSP violations, and more. 456 457 --- 458 459 ## Security 460 461 A one-page overview is in [`docs/SECURITY.md`](docs/SECURITY.md). Highlights: 462 463 - **Ownership checks** are part of the database query, so another owner's shop answers 404, the same as one that doesn't exist. 464 - **CSRF:** every state-changing request needs the app's Origin and a token bound to the session cookie. 465 - **Cookies** are `__Host-` prefixed, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax with no Domain, so shop subdomains never receive them. 466 - **Tokens** (sign-in, share, "Yes, I got it") are 32 random bytes and only their SHA-256 hash is stored. 467 - **Uploads** are size-capped, checked by content, and the price-list photo is never stored. 468 - **The certificate "ask" endpoint** is closed to the public at both Caddy and the app. 469 - **Privacy:** a customer's street address appears only on the owner's Orders page and in the order email, never in logs, evidence or the shared report. 470 471 --- 472 473 ## What's real today, and what isn't yet 474 475 Being honest about the state of a hackathon build: 476 477 **Real and running in production** 478 479 - The app at https://launchwitness.com on a GoDaddy Docker VPS, with Let's Encrypt HTTPS. 480 - A real shop launched by the app: its DNS record written through the GoDaddy API with a backup first, its certificate issued on demand, all seven checks proven, and a shareable report with an intact evidence chain. 481 - Real email: sign-in links, order emails and test orders sent through GoDaddy Professional Email, and test orders found in the inbox over IMAP. 482 - Monitoring, nightly database backups, and a tested restore. 483 - Private UPI: the live shops show UPI details only after an order, and customers can tell the shop they paid (UTR and an optional screenshot), which the seller checks before marking the order Paid. 484 485 **Not done yet** 486 487 - **Real launches on the seller's own domain** were cut for this round. They work in practice mode; real launches use a free `.launchwitness.com` address. 488 - **Creating a mailbox for each seller** through GoDaddy's email API is still a stub. Test orders go to the app's own mailbox, or the owner confirms with "Yes, I got it". 489 - **The admin** is whoever controls the `ADMIN_EMAIL` inbox. There is no second factor yet. 490 - **The demo fault** is staged so it shows reliably on camera. The detection and the fix are real. 491 - **Payments** are UPI links only. No money passes through LaunchWitness, so it never confirms a payment: "Customer says paid" stays a claim until the seller checks their UPI app. Card payments (a gateway, after the seller's KYC) are future work. 492 493 --- 494 495 ## How it was built 496 497 The whole product was built in **Claude Code**, over recorded sessions, each following a fixed ritual written in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md): 498 499 1. Read the progress file and propose a plan mapped to the acceptance criteria in [`docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`](docs/BUILD_PLAN.md). 500 2. Wait for the owner's OK before coding. 501 3. Make small, tested commits. 502 4. Update [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](docs/PROGRESS.md) and [`docs/BUILD_LOG.md`](docs/BUILD_LOG.md), then save a transcript that is redacted and secret-scanned before it is committed. 503 504 Product decisions (scope, safety rules, budget, what to postpone) stayed with the human. When the spec didn't answer something, the simplest option was chosen and recorded under "Decisions". A few hard rules held across every session: no secrets in the repo, Claude Code never spends money, GoDaddy defaults to the sandbox, and live Claude calls during development were kept to a minimum by using saved responses. 505 506 Every feature session ended with a check in a real browser at phone width, which caught real bugs. The full record is replayed at **https://launchwitness.com/build**, and a human-written summary of each session is in [`docs/BUILD_LOG.md`](docs/BUILD_LOG.md). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## What's next 511 512 1. **Run on the seller's own GoDaddy account**, so they own everything and monitoring matters most. 513 2. **Own-domain launches and per-seller mailboxes**, using the guarded purchase path and GoDaddy's email API. 514 3. **Change detection:** when a setting changes, ask "Was this you? Tap to restore" instead of fixing silently. 515 4. **A `/verify` page** backed by a DNS TXT record, so buyers can tell a seller's real shop from a fake using their name. 516 5. **More trades and languages:** bookings for salons and tutors, more Indian languages for the description. 517 6. **Card payments** ("Connect Razorpay") after the seller's KYC. 518 519 --- 520 521 ## Further reading 522 523 | Document | What's in it | 524 |---|---| 525 | [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) | The full product spec | 526 | [`docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`](docs/BUILD_PLAN.md) | Milestones and acceptance criteria | 527 | [`docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md`](docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md) | Every check scenario, its wording, and the test that proves it | 528 | [`docs/SECURITY.md`](docs/SECURITY.md) | Security on one page | 529 | [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](docs/PROGRESS.md) | Status, decisions and open questions | 530 | [`docs/BUILD_LOG.md`](docs/BUILD_LOG.md) | One entry per build session | 531 | [`docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`](docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md) | Going live on the VPS, step by step | 532 | [`deploy/README.md`](deploy/README.md) | The Docker setup in detail | 533 | [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) | Running the end-to-end tests | 534 535 --- 536 537

| Agent | Claude or code | Job | |---|---|---| | **Reader** | Claude | Description + price list → profile + copy + look | | **Namer** | Claude suggests, code checks | Available names with real prices | | **Policy** | Claude decides, code holds | OK to go live, or hold for a human | | **Planner** | Code | Every step, every before → after setting, and the cost → the approval card | | **Executor** | Code | Runs the approved plan with the guards, backup first, resumable step log | | **Checker** | Code | Address, HTTPS, email settings, real test order, clean finish | | **Doctor** | Claude chooses, code applies | Investigate, explain, pick a playbook fix, re-check | ### Design decisions worth knowing - **Every outside service sits behind one wrapper with a fake.** GoDaddy, Claude, SMTP, IMAP, DNS and HTTPS each have a real and an in-memory implementation (`app/integrations.py`). Practice mode (`USE_FAKES=true`) and the whole test suite run against the fakes, and tests block every real network call. - **Practice and real launches run the same code.** Practice swaps the outside world for fakes; the shop page, order handler and checks are identical, and every practice row is labelled. - **One A record per shop, no wildcard.** Each real shop gets exactly one DNS record written by the app, so a shop that doesn't exist doesn't resolve. - **SQLite on purpose.** One VPS, one app process (the app refuses to start a second), WAL mode, online backups (7 daily + 4 weekly) with a tested restore. Moving to Postgres is a small change because every table is a SQLModel model. - **The checker can't be turned into a weapon.** It reaches websites only through `SafeWeb`: it resolves the host once, refuses private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses, pins the checked IP, and re-checks every redirect. - **The app container uses public DNS resolvers.** The VPS's own resolvers returned wrong answers for some domains during testing, so the app asks 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 instead. --- ## Tech stack | Layer | Technology | |---|---| | Backend | Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLModel + SQLite, httpx, dnspython, APScheduler, Jinja2, Pillow, segno (QR codes), `anthropic` SDK | | Frontend | React 18, Vite 5, TypeScript, plain CSS (no UI kit) | | Seller sites | Server-rendered Jinja2, one template, six themes, self-hosted open-licence fonts | | Infrastructure | GoDaddy Docker VPS, Docker Compose, Caddy (automatic HTTPS, on-demand TLS) | | Email | GoDaddy Professional Email over SMTP and IMAP; Mailpit for the local stack | | Testing | pytest (1,580+ backend tests), Playwright end-to-end flows, ruff | --- ## Repository layout ``` backend/ app/ main.py FastAPI app, routers, host-based shop routing config.py settings from environment variables models.py, db.py SQLite tables (Business, Plan, DnsBackup, Evidence, AuditEvent, Approval, ...) agents/ reader, namer, policy, doctor, investigator (Claude); planner, executor, checker, launch_check, playbook (code) checks/ DNS lookups, HTTPS probes, email-settings checks, SSRF-safe fetch godaddy/ GoDaddy API client (ote|prod, scoped DNS writes), availability, email, rate limit sites/ shop rendering, themes, orders, fulfilment rules, templates, fonts mail/ SMTP, IMAP, email layout monitor/ scheduler for light monitoring safety/ spend guard, access control, CSRF/origin guard, route table proof.py, chain.py evidence rows and the hash chain outbox.py every email saved first, then sent and retried routers/ API routes (auth, businesses, launch, report, admin, watch, ...) tests/ pytest suite + fixtures (saved Claude responses, sample sellers) frontend/ React + Vite app (landing, describe, review, launch, report, orders, admin) e2e/ Playwright end-to-end tests deploy/ Dockerfile, docker-compose files, Caddyfile (local) and Caddyfile.prod scripts/ backups, checks, demo seeding, screenshots, secret scan, replay builder docs/ spec, build plan, progress, build log, security, checks matrix, runbooks, screenshots replay/ redacted Claude Code session transcripts (served at /build) ``` --- ## Running it yourself ### Option 1: practice mode on your machine (no keys needed) Practice mode uses in-memory fakes for GoDaddy, DNS, the mailbox and HTTPS, and saved Claude responses, so you don't need any API keys. ```bash cp .env.example .env # defaults are safe: fakes on, sandbox, purchases off python3.12 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt (cd frontend && npm install && npm run build) cd backend ../.venv/bin/pytest -q # run the tests (no network) ../.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000 ``` Open http://localhost:8000. For local development set `DEV_MODE=true` in `.env` so sign-in links appear on screen instead of being emailed (it refuses to start on https). `cd frontend && npm run dev` runs the frontend with hot reload and proxies `/api` to port 8000. > **On Windows**, use `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` and `.venv/Scripts/python -m uvicorn ...` instead. ### Option 2: the full stack with Docker ```bash docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build # → http://localhost ``` A production-like stack (real HTTPS through Caddy's local certificate authority, `DEV_MODE=false`, fakes, and Mailpit to catch emails at http://localhost:8025): ```bash docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml \ -f deploy/docker-compose.local.yml up -d --build --wait # → https://launchwitness.localhost bash scripts/check_m1.sh --local # automated checks of the running stack ``` ### Option 3: production on a VPS Follow [`docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`](docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md) and [`docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md`](docs/NEXT_SESSION_VPS.md). In short: fill `.env` on the server (never in the repo), then ```bash docker compose --env-file .env -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build bash scripts/check_m1.sh ``` Backups: `bash scripts/backup_db.sh` (7 daily + 4 weekly), restore with `bash scripts/restore_db.sh `. ### Rehearsing the demo ```bash python3 scripts/seed_demo.py --launched # creates Meera's shop and runs a practice launch python3 scripts/seed_demo.py --reset # removes it ``` To show the Doctor at work, sign in as the team (`ADMIN_EMAIL`), open a shop's report, and use the demo switch to stage a fault: the address leads nowhere, a parked page, a broken padlock, or a refused mail sign-in. The fault is staged so the demo is reliable; detecting and fixing it is real code. ### Key environment variables All are listed in [`.env.example`](.env.example) with safe defaults. | Variable | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `USE_FAKES` | `true` | Use in-memory fakes for every outside service | | `GODADDY_ENV` | `ote` | GoDaddy sandbox; `prod` only when set explicitly | | `ALLOW_PURCHASE` | `false` | Purchases are impossible unless turned on | | `MAX_SPEND_USD` | `15` | Hard limit on any single purchase | | `CLAUDE_MODE` | `fixture` | `fixture` uses saved responses; `live` calls the API | | `CLAUDE_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` | `3` | Live Claude calls stop when reached | | `DNS_MODE` | `per_shop` | One A record per shop (or `wildcard`) | | `MONITOR_ENABLED` | `true` | Background monitoring (tests never start it) | | `MAX_LIVE_SHOPS` | `40` | Upper limit on real shops | --- ## Testing ```bash cd backend && ../.venv/bin/pytest -q # 1,580+ tests, no network access allowed .venv/bin/python -m ruff check backend # lint cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npx playwright test bash scripts/secret_scan.sh # secrets in the repo and the whole git history ``` What the tests cover, among other things: - **Every check scenario** in [`docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md`](docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md): about forty website and email situations, each with the exact wording shown, how sure it is, and what the Doctor may do. - **Access control:** every owner route tested as owner, another seller, a guest, logged out and admin. A test fails if any route is missing from the route table. - **XSS:** a hostile string in every free-text field, every product field and the order form, parsed with a real HTML parser, in every theme. - **SSRF:** private ranges, redirect re-checks, IP pinning, redirect loops. - **Safety guards:** purchases blocked without all three conditions, DNS writes refused without a backup or outside the database. - **The Claude agents** against saved real responses, including a prompt-injection seller and a handwritten price-list photo. - **End-to-end flows** in a real browser: a full seller journey, two sellers who must not see each other's shops, guest practice, sign-in, legal pages, every theme launched in practice with no console errors or CSP violations, and more. --- ## Security A one-page overview is in [`docs/SECURITY.md`](docs/SECURITY.md). Highlights: - **Ownership checks** are part of the database query, so another owner's shop answers 404, the same as one that doesn't exist. - **CSRF:** every state-changing request needs the app's Origin and a token bound to the session cookie. - **Cookies** are `__Host-` prefixed, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax with no Domain, so shop subdomains never receive them. - **Tokens** (sign-in, share, "Yes, I got it") are 32 random bytes and only their SHA-256 hash is stored. - **Uploads** are size-capped, checked by content, and the price-list photo is never stored. - **The certificate "ask" endpoint** is closed to the public at both Caddy and the app. - **Privacy:** a customer's street address appears only on the owner's Orders page and in the order email, never in logs, evidence or the shared report. --- ## What's real today, and what isn't yet Being honest about the state of a hackathon build: **Real and running in production** - The app at https://launchwitness.com on a GoDaddy Docker VPS, with Let's Encrypt HTTPS. - A real shop launched by the app: its DNS record written through the GoDaddy API with a backup first, its certificate issued on demand, all seven checks proven, and a shareable report with an intact evidence chain. - Real email: sign-in links, order emails and test orders sent through GoDaddy Professional Email, and test orders found in the inbox over IMAP. - Monitoring, nightly database backups, and a tested restore. - Private UPI: the live shops show UPI details only after an order, and customers can tell the shop they paid (UTR and an optional screenshot), which the seller checks before marking the order Paid. **Not done yet** - **Real launches on the seller's own domain** were cut for this round. They work in practice mode; real launches use a free `.launchwitness.com` address. - **Creating a mailbox for each seller** through GoDaddy's email API is still a stub. Test orders go to the app's own mailbox, or the owner confirms with "Yes, I got it". - **The admin** is whoever controls the `ADMIN_EMAIL` inbox. There is no second factor yet. - **The demo fault** is staged so it shows reliably on camera. The detection and the fix are real. - **Payments** are UPI links only. No money passes through LaunchWitness, so it never confirms a payment: "Customer says paid" stays a claim until the seller checks their UPI app. Card payments (a gateway, after the seller's KYC) are future work. --- ## How it was built The whole product was built in **Claude Code**, over recorded sessions, each following a fixed ritual written in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md): 1. Read the progress file and propose a plan mapped to the acceptance criteria in [`docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`](docs/BUILD_PLAN.md). 2. Wait for the owner's OK before coding. 3. Make small, tested commits. 4. Update [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](docs/PROGRESS.md) and [`docs/BUILD_LOG.md`](docs/BUILD_LOG.md), then save a transcript that is redacted and secret-scanned before it is committed. Product decisions (scope, safety rules, budget, what to postpone) stayed with the human. When the spec didn't answer something, the simplest option was chosen and recorded under "Decisions". A few hard rules held across every session: no secrets in the repo, Claude Code never spends money, GoDaddy defaults to the sandbox, and live Claude calls during development were kept to a minimum by using saved responses. Every feature session ended with a check in a real browser at phone width, which caught real bugs. The full record is replayed at **https://launchwitness.com/build**, and a human-written summary of each session is in [`docs/BUILD_LOG.md`](docs/BUILD_LOG.md). --- ## What's next 1. **Run on the seller's own GoDaddy account**, so they own everything and monitoring matters most. 2. **Own-domain launches and per-seller mailboxes**, using the guarded purchase path and GoDaddy's email API. 3. **Change detection:** when a setting changes, ask "Was this you? Tap to restore" instead of fixing silently. 4. **A `/verify` page** backed by a DNS TXT record, so buyers can tell a seller's real shop from a fake using their name. 5. **More trades and languages:** bookings for salons and tutors, more Indian languages for the description. 6. **Card payments** ("Connect Razorpay") after the seller's KYC. --- ## Further reading | Document | What's in it | |---|---| | [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) | The full product spec | | [`docs/BUILD_PLAN.md`](docs/BUILD_PLAN.md) | Milestones and acceptance criteria | | [`docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md`](docs/CHECKS_MATRIX.md) | Every check scenario, its wording, and the test that proves it | | [`docs/SECURITY.md`](docs/SECURITY.md) | Security on one page | | [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](docs/PROGRESS.md) | Status, decisions and open questions | | [`docs/BUILD_LOG.md`](docs/BUILD_LOG.md) | One entry per build session | | [`docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md`](docs/RUNBOOK_M1.md) | Going live on the VPS, step by step | | [`deploy/README.md`](deploy/README.md) | The Docker setup in detail | | [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) | Running the end-to-end tests | ---
